findings.defect: SUPERSEDED, by material now in frontier.tex. The route leaves open "the least k for B^2 is 1 or 2" and proposes a further search. The paper's own prop:b2-realised (commit e90d01b, 2026-09-03 02:55, added after the route ran) settles it: k = 1, and not combinatorially but BY A GAME. I built the profile cube of that 138-vertex game (5 Max, 1 Min) from its printed harmonic normal form in exact arithmetic: it is profile-nondegenerate (no tie at any of the 384 incidences), a USO, ACYCLIC, HOLT-KLEE, of BA height 9 on the 6-cube, and its sink projection along the single Min coordinate is exactly B^2 (height 10, non-HK). So B^2 IS the k=1 sink projection of an acyclic Holt-Klee USO. The route's negative measurement is not contradicted -- it required both layers within Hamming distance 7 of B^2, and the true layers are at distance 6 and 9 -- the search radius was one unit too small on one layer. Integrating sproj:b2's "left open" clause would put a stale open question three pages from the proposition that answers it. It also means the route's whole b2hunt/b2pool/b2csp effort was spent re-deriving, at a smaller radius, something the round had already produced with a game.

The 16 cyclic USOs, which the route names for emphasis ("the 16 cyclic ones included"), are all Holt-Klee, so they are in the trivial case too. The genuinely non-trivial cases the route discharges are therefore THREE orientations: the two non-HK classes of the 3-cube and s_{G#} at m = 4 (plus, now, B^2 at m = 5, which comes free from prop:b2-realised). findings.defect: THE INTENDED OBSTRUCTION COULD NOT HAVE BITTEN EVEN IF THE GAP WERE PROVED, for a reason the route does not state. sproj:lcp and sproj:hk-bigcube require PROFILE-nondegeneracy -- no tie at any of the |C|*2^{|C|} incidences, Min's included -- which is strictly stronger than the paper's nondegeneracy (def:improvement-uso, Max ties only). def:ssg permits parallel edges, so a Min vertex whose two actions have equal harmonic rows makes every profile flat in that coordinate while leaving the Max cube nondegenerate; the profile cube must then be resolved by thm:flat-resolution, and that resolution is a combinatorial completion, not an LCP orientation, so Holt-Klee is not available -- exactly the caveat the paper already records for the one-player case in rem:oneplayer-lp. So the necessary condition "s realisable with k Min vertices => s is a k-fold sink projection of a Holt-Klee USO" is established only for profile-nondegenerate realisations; degenerate two-player realisations escape it entirely. The route's sproj:big-uso(b) supplies the resolution but never asks whether it is Holt-Klee.

findings.defect: NOVELTY CLAIM DOUBTFUL, and contradicted by the paper's own attribution. The route attributes the whole LCP chain but reserves clause (c) -- "the identification of the pivot orientation with the improving-switch orientation" -- as "what is new here". From memory (unchecked, no web): that identification is precisely how the LCP-USO correspondence is stated for games in Gaertner-Ruest (SSGs and P-matrix GLCPs) and Jurdzinski-Savani (discounted games), where complementary bases ARE strategy profiles and the induced orientation IS the improving-switch orientation; it is not an extra step one adds to Stickney-Watson. frontier.tex's own rem:lcp already treats it as prior art: "Stickney and Watson for the LCP-orientation correspondence this document meets again in prop:allsw-auso". findings.defect: Half of the four-signature claim is lem:duality. The dual game G-bar has the SAME profile cube, not a related one: q-bar^{v,a} = 1 - sum_w p^{v,a}_w - q^{v,a} gives f-bar_{v,a}(1-y) = 1 - f_{v,a}(y), and swapping the owner inverts the out-test a second time, so the out-set at every profile is unchanged. Hence (m,k) realisable <=> (k,m) realisable with the identical orientation, and "every signature in {(3,0),(2,1),(1,2),(0,3)}" is two independent claims, not four. This is the project's recurring lem:duality restatement, in a new place.

verdict:
HONEST AND CORRECT, BUT THIN, AND ITS CENTRAL NEGATIVE FINDING IS A COMBINATORIAL SHADOW OF SOMETHING THE PAPER ALREADY HAS WITH GAMES. I found no false mathematical statement: I re-verified, from scratch and in exact rational arithmetic, sproj:lcp (all clauses, all base profiles), sproj:handicap, sproj:cycle-dies, sproj:m3 (all 19 classes), sproj:seven-k1 (the 5-cube witness), and all 15 stored witnesses of sproj:c3. What fails is significance.

The route set out to supply an obstruction (Holt-Klee on the profile cube) and found it vacuous. But the paper had already established the substantive version of that twice, with actual games rather than combinatorics: cor:seven-two-player + prop:auso-seven show the non-HK height-7 orientation IS realised with k = 2, and prop:b2-realised shows a non-HK orientation realised with k = 1. Once you hold a game, "the necessary condition is satisfiable" is strictly weaker information. What the route adds beyond that is one witness (sproj:seven-k1: HK does not forbid k = 1 for the height-7 orbit at m = 4) and the observation that at m <= 3 one coordinate always suffices -- where, I showed, 17 of the 19 classes fall to a trivial hypersink prism, so the real content is three orientations. Meanwhile prop:b2-realised, added to the paper hours after the route ran, answers the route's own open question in the affirmative: I verified its 138-vertex game's profile cube is a profile-nondegenerate acyclic HOLT-KLEE USO of the 6-cube projecting along its one Min coordinate exactly onto B^2. That is a datum the paper does not yet record and should.

Circularity/vacuity checks: no algorithm, no oracle, no claimed polynomial class, no claimed lower-bound family, so those tests do not apply. The route claims the ABSENCE of a barrier, and it is right to; but note that the barrier it removes covered none of M1, M2, M2T, M3, M4, M5, M6 or def:bsi -- it was never a constraint on any mechanism, only on the realisability search.

THE REAL REMAINING GAP, more precisely than the route states it. The route's gap ("every USO of the m-cube is the sink projection along one coordinate of a Holt-Klee USO of the (m+1)-cube") is the wrong gap: proving it would say nothing about games, and by finding 5 above it would not even be a necessary condition for degenerate realisations. The true gap is unchanged by this route and is now sharper than when the route started: EXHIBIT SUBSTOCHASTIC TRANSIENT Q_0, Q_1 OVER C = Vmax u Vmin WITH |Vmin| AND THE DYADIC PRECISION GROWING ADDITIVELY IN j, WHOSE PROFILE CUBE'S SINK PROJECTION ALONG Vmin IS THE j-TH BLOW-UP LEVEL B^j FOR j >= 3 (dimension 7, height 22) -- prop:b2-realised does j = 2 at a cost of two Max, one Min and three bits of precision, and Holt-Klee is now known, from that same game's profile cube, to be no obstruction there.

INTEGRATION: as written, WORSE. 666 lines and 25 environments, of which one theorem duplicates prop:allsw-auso, one promotes an attributed prior-art sentence of rem:gsharp-bigcube into a load-bearing third external import (Gaertner-Morris-Ruest), one leaves an open question the paper answers three pages away, and several restate lem:duality or one-line constructions as censuses.

TRIMMED, SLIGHTLY BETTER -- integrate these six and nothing else, about two pages:
  (1) sproj:trichotomy + sproj:flat + sproj:facesink + sproj:big-uso. These carry lem:trichotomy, lem:flat-class(a),(b), lem:face-sink and thm:flat-resolution to the profile cube and let thm:cyclic-uso DROP its "from memory, unchecked" Stickney-Watson citation for the USO property, degenerate games included. Removing a citation is worth real points in this document.
  (2) sproj:contract + sproj:lcp(a),(b). A from-scratch proof that M is a P-matrix, so rem:lcp need not lean on Hansen & Ibsen-Jensen for it. Soften (c) to "the identification is presumably theirs too".
  (3) sproj:projection. Generalises prop:gsharp-bigcube's instance observation to every stopping SSG in two paragraphs. Keep, and state the profile-nondegeneracy hypothesis explicitly next to rem:oneplayer-lp's analogous caveat.
  (4) sproj:seven-k1, as one proposition with the outmap displayed. The route's one new fact.
  (5) ONE SENTENCE in rem:gsharp-bigcube: at m <= 3 every USO is a k = 1 projection of a Holt-Klee USO (17 of the 19 classes trivially, layer 0 = s as a hypersink); the height-7 orbit is one at m = 4; and B^2 is one at m = 5, WITNESSED BY prop:b2-realised's own profile cube (nondegenerate, acyclic, Holt-Klee, height 9). Then the honest conclusion: Holt-Klee constrains nothing once one Min vertex is present, so the two-player half of realisability is about the shape of M, not about the USO axioms.
  (6) ONE SENTENCE in rem:lcp: handicap 0 does not even imply acyclicity of the profile cube (thm:cyclic-uso's own game, minors 9/4, 1, 2, 351/256, 30047/16384, 287/256, 31/32).
DO NOT integrate: sproj:hk-bigcube as a theorem, sproj:proj-acyclic, sproj:proj-cyclic-general(b), sproj:b2, sproj:c3's negative half (GMR-dependent) -- though sproj:c3's positive half, 17 explicit realisations at |C| = 3, is worth a repository note with the duality collapse recorded -- and sproj:crossover / sproj:prism / sproj:2face, which are search machinery and belong in scripts.
